**Resubmitted — deviation, preferred level, minimality defect repaired.**

What changed from the prior submission:

- **Operative edit:** Section 12.4's restrictive sentence is now struck in full and replaced with "[Intentionally omitted.]" rather than rewritten as an affirmative permission. A bare `delete_paragraph` is rejected by the minimality gate, so the strike is expressed as a replace of the offending sentence only — the paragraph number is untouched, so no cross-reference dangles.
- **No duplicated permission:** the pro-Customer confirmation now rests solely on retained Section 12.3 ("Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service ... in any field or territory"), so the same right is not granted twice in operative text.
- **Coverage:** the sole preferred element ("Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.") is mapped to operation 1. Fallback scoping/timing/carve-out language is confined to the margin comment and not imported into the contract.
- **Untouched:** Section 13.4 use restrictions and Section 2.2 exclusivity (separate rule) remain as drafted.

Redline validated `ok:true` with clean minimality; finding submitted once.
